Population.evidence_source: [/page/3/Text/5] In order to explore the pathways to and from suicide attempts in the past and after release from prison, we carried out a qualitative interview study. We used the prison system as a point for obtaining our sample and interviewed 35 male offenders, aged 18–52, 1 week prior to and approximately 6 weeks after their release from a Category B medium secure prison in South-West England (Howerton et al. 2007).[/page/3/Text/6] We over-sampled young offenders and those categorised by the prison assessment care in custody teamwork system as being at risk of suicide.[/page/3/Text/7] The pre-release interview included questions about the participants' childhood and early history, methods of coping with stress and difficulties, previous suicide attempts, perception of their own mental health, and attitudes towards help seeking. The post-release interview included a discussion of recent life events, current mental distress and any suicidal thoughts or attempts following release.

Type.evidence_source: [/page/3/Text/5] In order to explore the pathways to and from suicide attempts in the past and after release from prison, we carried out a qualitative interview study. We used the prison system as a point for obtaining our sample and interviewed 35 male offenders, aged 18–52, 1 week prior to and approximately 6 weeks after their release from a Category B medium secure prison in South-West England (Howerton et al. 2007).[/page/3/Text/6] Initial interviews were semi-structured and carried out face-to-face.[/page/3/Text/8] All interviews were carried out by a medical sociologist (AH), and were taped and transcribed verbatim.

Area.evidence_source: [/page/3/Text/5] In order to explore the pathways to and from suicide attempts in the past and after release from prison, we carried out a qualitative interview study.[/page/3/Text/7] The pre-release interview included questions about the participants' childhood and early history, methods of coping with stress and difficulties, previous suicide attempts, perception of their own mental health, and attitudes towards help seeking. The post-release interview included a discussion of recent life events, current mental distress and any suicidal thoughts or attempts following release. We asked about the extent to which respondents felt in control of their lives and what plans they had for the future.[/page/3/Text/8] We assessed the degree of hesitancy in the participants' responses and the extent to which they articulated a level of learning from past experiences.
